plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value is irrational (you'd lose money if you win), and bidding significantly below your value risks losing to a slightly higher bid, even if it's below your true value. Since it's round 1 and there's no history, I will bid slightly below my value to test the waters.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $49, the expected value is $24.5. However, with only two other bidders, the second-highest bid will likely be lower. A conservative approach, given my value of $7, is to bid just enough to likely win against reasonable opponents. Bidding too high risks overpaying; bidding too low risks losing. I will bid $7.10.
